doc.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: Auditioning with Brubeck, Joe Morello and Eugene Wright
summary: At the audition with the original quartet he played new tunes and Kathy's Waltz, emulating Paul Desmond.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So I walk into the original quartet, which is like a dream, I mean I had memorized all those Desmond things and all that stuff. So I walked in and had done my homework on the new tunes. But I didn’t have to do my homework on the old tunes because I already knew them. So Dave says, “Well what do you want to play?” I said, “Anything you want. Anything you want to play.” And he tells this in his interviews now to people. So he says, “Play some of the new tunes” and I played them right out. That’s cool. And then they were fooling around with something and they started playing “Kathy’s Waltz” and I jumped on that one. And then there was another, I forget which other one we did of his tunes but I jumped on that one too and played that one. And I even was freaking him out once in a while, which Joe Morello told me later did freak him out, on a couple of other gigs we did for the Seeing Eye Dog Foundation with the original quartet, to raise money for them, where he says when he was playing and he closed his eyes and he had to kind of get into it but because I would emulate Paul he really would get like this bizarre feeling for a second of being back, you know, one of those type of things. But basically then we started fooling around with standards and doing a bunch of things, and whatever he wanted to play I played. I didn’t care what key, we didn’t talk about keys, he says, “All right, you’ve got the gig.” It was great. So I left. He never asked about the bread. Ever. Didn’t ask when I got the call for my first gigs. I went out and played them and didn’t ask. I got my checks in the mail. I had no idea what I was going to make and it made no difference whatsoever. None whatsoever. And that was a major break. Playing with Doc Severinsen, that was a major break, with the Tonight Show I sat in the orchestra here in Buffalo back, just as a contract player.
